lessons.title: Sustainable development and global citizenship
lessons.programRef: Cameroon anglophone secondary Citizenship Education syllabus, Form 4 — to be checked against the official text
lessons.author: CastBridge (AI draft)
lessons.source: Original writing following the Cameroonian curriculum; to be reviewed by a teacher
objectives: Describe its economic, social and environmental parts
Explain climate change and what individuals can do
reviewNotes: Teacher to verify: the SDG details (17 goals, 2015, 2030) and the statements on climate change impacts in Cameroon (kept deliberately general).

Draft for teacher review: content is general and non-political; legal ages, institutions, names of laws and any health or road-safety statement must be verified (by a teacher, and for health topics by a health worker) before release.

blocks.md: **Sustainable development** means meeting the needs of people today **without damaging the ability of future generations** to meet their own needs. It joins three parts: **economic** (jobs and growth), **social** (education, health, fairness) and **environmental** (clean air and water, forests, biodiversity). A project that gives income but destroys the forest or pollutes water is not sustainable.

blocks.caption: Where needs meet
blocks.alt: Two overlapping circles for people and planet with 'Fair growth' in the overlap.

blocks.title: Climate change
blocks.md: Burning **fossil fuels** (petrol, diesel, coal, gas) and clearing forests add **greenhouse gases** such as carbon dioxide to the air. These trap heat and cause **global warming**, which leads to more extreme weather: floods, droughts, irregular rains and rising sea levels. Cameroon's farmers, coasts and forests can be affected. Responses: **reduce** emissions, **adapt** (for example drought-resistant crops), and **protect forests**.

In 2015 world leaders at the UN agreed on **17 Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs)** to be reached by 2030. They include ending **poverty** and **hunger**, **good health**, **quality education**, **gender equality**, **clean water and sanitation**, **clean energy**, **decent work**, **climate action**, **life on land and below water**, **peace and justice** and **partnerships**. Governments, businesses, schools and individuals all have a part.

blocks.title: Global citizenship
blocks.md: A **global citizen** knows that people, economies and the environment are connected across the world, respects other cultures and acts responsibly at home and abroad. Everyday actions: save electricity and water, avoid waste, plant trees, buy local and sustainable goods, use public transport or walk, learn about other countries and support fair trade.

blocks.title: Common mistakes
blocks.md:
- Sustainable development is not 'no development': it is development that lasts.
- Climate change is not the same as the weather on one day.
- Individual actions matter, but laws and cooperation between countries are also needed.

blocks.title: Example 1: sustainable or not?
blocks.statement: A company clears a large forest to grow one crop and leaves the soil bare. Is this sustainable?
steps: But it destroys the forest and soil that people need later.
blocks.answer: No; it harms the environment for the future.

blocks.title: Example 2: personal action
blocks.statement: Give two things a pupil can do to reduce waste of energy.
steps: Switch off lights and appliances when not in use.
Use natural light and walk short distances.
blocks.answer: Switch off unused lights and walk short distances.

Explain responsible and lawful online behaviour

Draft for teacher review: content is general and non-political; legal ages, institutions, names of laws and any health or road-safety statement must be verified (by a teacher, and for health topics by a health worker) before release.

blocks.md: Mobile phones, the internet and social media help us to learn, communicate, work, trade and take part in public life. A **digital citizen** uses these tools safely, respectfully and lawfully. The same values as in the real world apply online: **honesty, respect, responsibility** and **care for others**.

blocks.caption: Four steps before sharing
blocks.alt: Four boxes: read, check the source, consider the effect, then decide.

blocks.title: Protect yourself
blocks.md:
- Use **strong passwords** (long, with letters, numbers and symbols) and never share them.
- Do not post your **address, phone number, ID numbers, school timetable** or private photos.
- Be careful with strangers: not everyone is who they claim to be.
- Beware of **scams**: messages asking for money, mobile-money PINs, or promising prizes.
- Log out of shared devices and keep software updated.

blocks.title: Respect and truth
blocks.md: **Cyberbullying** is insulting, threatening or humiliating someone online; it can cause deep harm and may be punishable. **Fake news** is false or misleading information shared as if true. Before sharing, **check the source**, look for other reports, and think about the effect on others. **Hate speech**, threats and spreading private photos without permission are harmful and unlawful.

**Responsible use**: respect others' ideas, give credit when you use someone else's work (avoid **plagiarism**), do not download or copy pirated material, report abuse to a trusted adult or the platform, and balance **screen time** with study, sleep, family and exercise. If someone threatens you or asks for private pictures, **stop, save the evidence, and tell a trusted adult**.

blocks.title: Common mistakes
blocks.md:
- Information that looks professional or is widely shared is not necessarily true.
- 'Deleting' a message does not guarantee it cannot be copied or shown.
- Sharing your password with a friend can lead to misuse of your account.

blocks.title: Example 1: spot the scam
blocks.statement: You receive a message: 'You won 1 000 000 FCFA! Send your mobile-money PIN to claim.' What should you do?
steps: Real organisations never ask for your PIN.
Do not reply and do not send any money or code.
blocks.answer: Ignore it, do not share your PIN, and report it.

blocks.title: Example 2: before sharing
blocks.statement: A message says a school will close tomorrow because of a disease. What should you check before forwarding it?
steps: Is it from an official source?
Do other reliable sources say the same?
If not confirmed, do not forward.
blocks.answer: Check the official source before forwarding.

lessons.title: Planning and carrying out a civic project
lessons.programRef: Cameroon anglophone secondary Citizenship Education syllabus, Form 4 — to be checked against the official text
lessons.author: CastBridge (AI draft)
lessons.source: Original writing following the Cameroonian curriculum; to be reviewed by a teacher
objectives: Identify a community problem and set a goal
Plan a project with tasks, roles and a budget
Work as a team and evaluate the results
reviewNotes: Teacher to adapt costs to local prices; all amounts are invented; safety rules should follow the school's policy.

Draft for teacher review: content is general and non-political; legal ages, institutions, names of laws and any health or road-safety statement must be verified (by a teacher, and for health topics by a health worker) before release.

blocks.md: A **civic project** is a planned activity by a group to solve a problem or improve life in the community, such as cleaning a stream, planting trees, building a school garden or teaching younger children to read. Carrying out such projects develops **teamwork, leadership, responsibility** and **respect for the community**. Everyone can contribute, including pupils.

blocks.caption: Steps of a civic project
blocks.alt: Four boxes showing find the problem, plan, carry out and evaluate.

blocks.title: Project steps
blocks.md:
1. **Identify the problem** (talk to people and observe).
2. **Set a clear goal**: what, where, when and for whom.
3. **Plan**: list tasks, assign roles, choose a timetable, list materials and **budget**.
4. **Get permission and support** from school, chiefs, council or parents.
5. **Carry out** the activity safely.
6. **Evaluate**: Did we reach the goal? What went well? What can we improve?
7. **Share** the results and thank those who helped.

blocks.title: Team roles
blocks.md: A team often has a **coordinator** (leads and keeps the timetable), a **secretary** (records decisions), a **treasurer** (keeps money records honestly and shows accounts), and **members** in charge of tasks such as publicity, materials and safety. All members are equal in value; decisions are made by discussion and, if needed, by vote.

**Volunteering** means giving time and effort freely for the benefit of others. Volunteers help the community, learn new skills, make friends and build a sense of belonging. Good volunteers are reliable, honest, respect people's dignity and follow safety and child-protection rules. **A budget** estimates costs: for example, tools and seedlings for a tree-planting day. The treasurer must record every payment and keep receipts.

blocks.title: Be careful
blocks.md:
- Always get permission before using land, tools or public places.
- Safety first: protect pupils from traffic, tools and weather.
- Money must be handled openly: record income and spending and show the accounts to the group.

blocks.title: Example 1: budget
blocks.statement: A class plans a tree-planting day: 40 seedlings at 250 FCFA each and 5 tools at 2 000 FCFA each. What is the total cost?

blocks.title: Example 2: evaluation
blocks.statement: After the tree-planting day, only 25 of the 40 trees were planted. What percentage of the goal was achieved?
steps: The group can plan to plant the rest and improve organisation.
